mainFieldChanges.before: idea:String.raw`The same additional unit is available to both consumers. Its total benefit is therefore the sum of their marginal benefits at that same G. In this economy, $MB_i(G)=\max\{0,a_i-b_iG\}$, so the efficient level solves the crossing of the piecewise-linear vertical sum with c, or is zero when the initial sum does not cover cost. For a private good at price p, instead add the individual quantities $q_i(p)=\max\{0,(a_i-p)/b_i\}$. These are different aggregation operations.`,
mainFieldChanges.after: idea:String.raw`The same additional unit is available to both consumers. Its total benefit is therefore the sum of their marginal benefits at that same G. In this economy, $MB_i(G)=\max\{0,a_i-b_iG\}$ with $a_i,b_i,c>0$, so the efficient level solves the crossing of the piecewise-linear vertical sum with c, or is zero when the initial sum does not cover cost. For a private good at price p, instead add the individual quantities $q_i(p)=\max\{0,(a_i-p)/b_i\}$. These are different aggregation operations.`,

mainFieldChanges.before:
statement:String.raw`A non-excludable benefit can be enjoyed without contributing to its provision. In the chosen one-shot game, n identical players choose nonnegative contributions gᵢ, total provision is G=Σgᵢ, and each receives $B(G)-cg_i$, with $B(G)=aG-bG^2/2$ up to satiation. The Nash total and efficient total are
$$G_N=\max\{0,(a-c)/b\},$$
$$G_S=\max\{0,(na-c)/(nb)\}.$$
For n>1 and a positive efficient level, voluntary provision can fall short.`,
mainFieldChanges.after:
statement:String.raw`A non-excludable benefit can be enjoyed without contributing to its provision. In the chosen one-shot game, n is a positive integer and a,b,c>0. The n identical players choose nonnegative contributions gᵢ, total provision is G=Σgᵢ, and each receives $B(G)-cg_i$, with $B(G)=aG-bG^2/2$ up to G=a/b and constant benefit thereafter. The Nash total and efficient total are
$$G_N=\max\{0,(a-c)/b\},$$
$$G_S=\max\{0,(na-c)/(nb)\}.$$
For n>1 and a positive efficient level, voluntary provision can fall short.`,

mainFieldChanges.before: idea:String.raw`A contributor pays the full marginal cost c but receives only their own marginal benefit a−bG. The planner counts n times that benefit. A player’s best response to others’ total H is max{0,G_N−H}. Thus any nonnegative vector summing to a positive G_N is Nash; the symmetric split shown here is one representative, not a unique contribution pattern. When G_N=0, all contributions are zero.`,
mainFieldChanges.after: idea:String.raw`A contributor pays the full marginal cost c but receives only their own marginal benefit a−bG. The planner counts n times that benefit. A player’s best response to others’ total H is $\max\{0,G_N-H\}$. Thus any nonnegative vector summing to a positive $G_N$ is Nash; the symmetric split shown here is one representative, not a unique contribution pattern. When $G_N$=0, all contributions are zero.`,

mainFieldChanges.before: idea:String.raw`An entrant compares their average product A−BN/2 with their cost. Their entry also reduces the returns to existing effort, a congestion effect they do not pay for. A resource owner instead compares marginal product A−BN with cost. The rent curve $R(N)=(A-c)N-BN^2/2$ peaks at N_S and returns to zero at N_OA.`,
mainFieldChanges.after: idea:String.raw`An entrant compares their average product A−BN/2 with their cost. Their entry also reduces the returns to existing effort, a congestion effect they do not pay for. A resource owner instead compares marginal product A−BN with cost. The rent curve $R(N)=(A-c)N-BN^2/2$ peaks at $N_S$ and returns to zero at $N_{OA}$.`,

mainFieldChanges.before:
statement:String.raw`A network externality occurs when the value of joining depends on how many others participate. The chosen fulfilled-expectations inverse demand is $p=vx(1-x)$ for adoption share x∈[0,1]. Under the explicitly chosen adjustment rule
$$\dot x=\kappa x[vx(1-x)-p],$$
positive fixed points exist when 4p≤v. With 0<4p<v, the lower fixed point is an unstable critical mass and the upper one is stable; zero is also stable.`,
mainFieldChanges.after:
statement:String.raw`A network externality occurs when the value of joining depends on how many others participate. The chosen fulfilled-expectations inverse demand is $p=vx(1-x)$ for adoption share x∈[0,1]. Take v>0, κ>0 and p≥0. Under the explicitly chosen adjustment rule
$$\dot x=\kappa x[vx(1-x)-p],$$
positive fixed points exist when 4p≤v. With 0<4p<v, the lower fixed point is an unstable critical mass and the upper one is stable; zero is also stable.`,

mainFieldChanges.before: idea:String.raw`Set A₀=5, a=20, h=a+(b+d)A₀ and price τ=a+bA₀. A cap fixes abatement at A_Q=A₀, while the price induces A_P=A₀−u/b. Full information gives A*=A₀−u/(b+d). Integrating the marginal-benefit/cost gap gives $L_Q=u^2/[2(b+d)]$ and $L_P=u^2d^2/[2b^2(b+d)]$. Take expectations and subtract. The chosen uniform shock support ±0.8ρbA₀ keeps all outcomes strictly inside capacity 10.`,
mainFieldChanges.after: idea:String.raw`Set A₀=5, a=20, h=a+(b+d)A₀ and price τ=a+bA₀. A cap fixes abatement at $A_Q=A_0$, while the price induces $A_P=A_0-u/b$. Full information gives A*=A₀−u/(b+d). Integrating the marginal-benefit/cost gap gives $L_Q=u^2/[2(b+d)]$ and $L_P=u^2d^2/[2b^2(b+d)]$. Take expectations and subtract. The chosen uniform shock support ±0.8ρbA₀ keeps all outcomes strictly inside capacity 10.`,

mainFieldChanges.before:
idea:String.raw`The displayed special case has $u_i=\log x_i+a_i\log(1+G)$ and resource constraint $x_A+x_B+cG=R$. For weight λ∈(0,1), let A=λa_A+(1−λ)a_B. Maximizing the weighted utility sum gives
$$G^*=\max\{0,g_0\},$$
$$g_0=\frac{AR-c}{c(A+1)},$$
with x_A=λ(R−cG*) and x_B=(1−λ)(R−cG*). Compute $\operatorname{MRS}_i=a_i x_i/(1+G)$ to verify the sum condition, or its zero-provision inequality. Lower A’s reported taste while either holding allocation fixed or replanning from reports: the two experiments distinguish an informational shortfall from an actual allocation change.`,
mainFieldChanges.after:
idea:String.raw`The displayed special case has $u_i=\log x_i+a_i\log(1+G)$ and resource constraint $x_A+x_B+cG=R$. Here $a_i,c,R>0$, private consumption satisfies $x_i>0$, and $G\ge0$. For weight λ∈(0,1), let $A=\lambda a_A+(1-\lambda)a_B$. Maximizing the weighted utility sum gives
$$G^*=\max\{0,g_0\},$$
$$g_0=\frac{AR-c}{c(A+1)},$$
with $x_A=\lambda(R-cG^*)$ and $x_B=(1-\lambda)(R-cG^*)$. Compute $\operatorname{MRS}_i=a_i x_i/(1+G)$ to verify the sum condition, or its zero-provision inequality. Lower A’s reported taste while either holding allocation fixed or replanning from reports: the two experiments distinguish an informational shortfall from an actual allocation change.`,
